title: A Cache/Algorithm Co-design for Parallel Real-Time Systems with Data Dependency on Multi/Many-core System-on-Chips
problem: Conventional shared caches suffer from intensive interference in parallel real-time systems, and existing cache management techniques only ensure determinism for single-threaded tasks, not for data-dependent parallel workloads.
motivation: Parallel real-time systems require efficient mechanisms to manage shared cache resources and reduce data transmission latency while meeting strict timing constraints.
method: The approach designs a virtual indexed, physically tagged, selectively-inclusive, non-exclusive L1.5 Cache with way-level control and fine-grained sharing capabilities. A scheduling algorithm for DAG tasks exploits the L1.5 Cache to reduce inter-core data transmission and makespan. The solution spans from SoC architecture and ISA design through the programming model.
key_novelty: A selectively-inclusive, non-exclusive L1.5 Cache with way-level control that enables both interference isolation and efficient data sharing for DAG-based parallel tasks in real-time systems.
contributions: Virtual indexed, physically tagged L1.5 Cache architecture with way-level control for parallel real-time systems
DAG task scheduling algorithm that exploits the L1.5 Cache structure to minimize data transmission and makespan
End-to-end system implementation from SoC design, ISA, to programming model
Experimental validation showing significant timing performance improvements with negligible overhead

metrics.speedup: makespan reduction for DAG task execution

limitations: Paper does not discuss applicability to non-DAG workloads or provide detailed comparisons with other recent cache coherence and management techniques.
primary_theme: Cache-algorithm co-design for real-time parallel task scheduling
